fields.description:
# s3 doctor heals into whatever branch the tracker has checked out, publishing unrelated commits

## The originally-filed mechanism is DISPROVEN

This ticket was filed claiming `_publish_and_prune` bundles a literal `HEAD` and so "silently
carries the WRONG tip alongside the correct `refs/heads/<ref>`". Running the real
`heal_multi_bundle` against the existing harness, with a tracker whose checked-out branch is NOT
the published ref, disproves that: the produced bundle lists `HEAD` and `refs/heads/tickets` at
the SAME commit.

They cannot diverge in one non-racy heal. `_fold_heads` merges every fetched head INTO the
worktree's HEAD and returns `merged_sha = git rev-parse HEAD`; `_publish_and_prune` then runs
`git branch -f <ref> <merged_sha>` in exactly the `current_branch != ref` case the original
write-up called defective. The ref is force-moved onto whatever commit HEAD names, so the two
bundle entries always agree. A test written to the original acceptance criteria would PASS
before any fix — there is no RED, and changing the bundle argument fixes nothing.

Two supporting sub-claims are also unreachable: an unborn HEAD never reaches the bundle step
(`git merge` fast-forwards it first), and a detached HEAD on the ref's own history bundles
correctly.

## The real defect

The same probe shows what IS broken. With a side branch checked out carrying one unrelated
commit, that commit ends up reachable from the published tickets tip. Because the fold merges
into the worktree HEAD, the side branch's history is merged into the tickets history, and
`branch -f` then publishes it as the tickets ref. The wrong content reaches the ref through
`_fold_heads` + `branch -f`, never through the bundle argument.

The doctor's whole design assumes the tracker has the published ref checked out. That holds for
rebar's own stores, so the defect is latent today — but when it does not hold, the heal silently
writes unrelated commits into the shared ticket history, which is a data-integrity failure that
no caller can detect after the fact.

## Scope: refuse loudly, do not silently mis-heal

Fixing the fold to target `refs/heads/<ref>` properly is a design change, not a bugfix: you
cannot `git merge` into a non-checked-out branch, so it needs `merge-tree`/`commit-tree` or a
scratch worktree. That rework is filed SEPARATELY and is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE here.

This ticket closes the silent-corruption door only: when the tracker is not on the published
ref, the heal REFUSES before touching anything, and says why. The refusal raises the module's
existing `S3DoctorConflict`, which is the established loud channel — the sole caller
(`_store/push.py`) already logs it with its hint and escalates under `strict`. Silent failures
have bitten this project before, so a skipped-with-a-reason return is deliberately NOT the
chosen shape.

The guard runs before any bundle is downloaded, and AFTER the existing single-bundle no-op
check, so a store with nothing to heal keeps returning its no-op result unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A heal on a tracker whose checked-out branch is not the published ref raises
      `S3DoctorConflict` instead of merging.
- [ ] That refusal happens before any bundle is downloaded or merged.
- [ ] The remote bundles are left exactly as they were found when the heal refuses.
- [ ] No commit from the checked-out side branch becomes reachable from the published ref.
- [ ] A detached-HEAD tracker is refused by the same guard.
- [ ] The refusal's hint names the required tracker state, so an operator can act on it.
- [ ] A tracker correctly on the published ref still heals losslessly (existing behaviour
      unchanged), and a single-bundle store still returns its no-op result.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the refusal and the pollution it prevents; they fail before the
      change.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck` and the s3_doctor test tiers pass.
